Vulnérabilité critique CVE-2026-111357 affectant Ivanti.

CISA added two new Ivanti Connect Secure vulnerabilities (CVE-2026-111357, CVE-2026-118527) to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog.

CVE-2026-111357, a missing authentication for a critical function vulnerability that allows a local authenticated attacker to escalate their privileges, and CVE-2026-118527, a “Generation of Predictable Numbers or Identifiers Vulnerability” that makes remote authenticated file upload possible, have been exploited as zero-days in conjunction with a third flaw: CVE-2026-104935, an authentication bypass and RCE vulnerability.

According to Volexity researchers, who discovered the attack and reported it to Ivanti, the attackers were covertly turning the SSL VPN appliances into a foothold in the targeted organizations’ network.

“Because the operation was detected and disrupted, the threat actor’s ultimate objectives could not be determined. However, Volexity assesses with high confidence that UTA0576’s actions signaled preparation for lateral movement and a broader compromise of the victim network,” the researchers said.

The attackers engaged in credential theft and queried Active Directory for Windows LAPS passwords and BitLocker recovery keys, Rapid7 researchers noted .

CISA has ordered US federal civilian agencies to address CVE-2026-111357 by November 2, 2026, and to engage in forensic triage and investigate for possible compromise. CVE-2026-118527 has a November 13 deadline.

All three flaws have been fixed by Ivanti, and customers using the Connect Secure SSL VPN appliance are advised to implement the provided updates.

items.detail:
Incident de sécurité rapporté par The Record.

A recent post by the BYOD gang appears to line up with a security incident that prompted campus-wide action at Michigan State University. BYOD drew attention in October for an attack on the University of New Mexico.

Michigan State University officials said recent claims by a ransomware gang were tied to an incident last month that forced password resets for all student and employee accounts.

On Sunday evening, the BYOD ransomware gang added the university to its leak site — claiming to have stolen personal information on 1.3 million current and former students. Last week, BYOD caused outrage after attacking The University of New Mexico and shutting down its hospital.

A spokesperson for Michigan State told Recorded Future News that the university “became aware of suspicious cyber activity and immediately began investigating the matter,” in early October.

To protect university accounts and systems, the school’s IT team required anyone with an MSU NetID to reset their passwords and create a new password that is at least 15 characters long. The email was sent out to campus on October 1.

“Based on the investigation to date, the activity appeared to be a potential credential compromise event. Current evidence does not indicate a successful compromise of the university's central Active Directory environment,” a spokesperson said.

“There is no evidence that other MSU data was accessed, changed, or stolen, and the university's security measures continue to function as designed.”

Incident de sécurité rapporté par The Record.

Blockchain security companies said more than $46 million left the Mercado Bitcoin platform.

Brazilian cryptocurrency platform Mercado Bitcoin suspended all deposits and withdrawals after a cybersecurity incident on Monday morning.

In messages on social media, Mercado Bitcoin said the cyberattack did not harm customers and did not lead to a data breach.

Cybersecurity for smaller businesses often suffers by being either underpowered or too complex. This tension can be challenging to resolve for small IT teams that may lack an in-house cyber expert. Understanding the problem is not the same as understanding where the solution lies.

Effective SMB protection demands that vendors lead their customers through a clear onboarding process – and offer practical and transparent guidance during incident response engagements.

Some 88% of the critical and high-severity weaknesses found in live attack tests on enterprise environments this year would not have been identified through vendor advisories or other outside sources, new data has suggested.

The figure comes from a report published on November 2 by Armadin, the offensive security startup launched by Mandiant founder Kevin Mandia, based on AI-driven attacks against its clients' live systems.

The clients span nearly a dozen industries, but Armadin did not disclose how many organizations or findings the data covers.

Read more on exposure management: AI Threats and Alert Fatigue Challenge Cybersecurity Teams

Defects in software the clients had written themselves made up 67% of the critical findings and 78% of the high findings that advisories could not cover. Vendor products deployed in ways no advisory describes, such as administrative consoles exposed to the internet, accounted for 24% and 22%.

The remaining 9% of critical findings, and under 1% of high ones, were zero-days Armadin found itself, including one in an identity governance platform whose vendor took almost four months to issue an advisory.

items.detail:
Signal de veille — Silicon.fr.

Cinq organisations représentant des éditeurs de contenus numériques français ont déposé, le 29 octobre 2026, une plainte auprès de la Commission européenne contre les pratiques de Google liées à AI Overviews (AIO) et AI Mode (AIM). Cette démarche collective vise moins à obtenir une réparation immédiate qu’à alimenter l’instruction d’une enquête déjà ouverte par Bruxelles afin de déterminer si Google a enfreint les règles de concurrence de l’Union en utilisant des contenus d’éditeurs web et des vidéos YouTube pour ses services d’IA, notamment sans compensation appropriée ni possibilité effective de refus. Les cinq organisations françaises entendent donc fournir à la Commission des éléments factuels recueillis depuis le déploiement français. Leur contribution porte sur les effets observés sur la visibilité, les marques, le trafic et les conditions de concurrence, dans un contexte où Google reste un point d’accès déterminant aux audiences. Une coalition inédite d’éditeurs La plainte réunit le CPA, la FNPS, le GESTE, le SEPM et le SPIIL. Ces organisations couvrent un spectre large de l’édition numérique : presse d’information spécialisée, presse magazine, presse indépendante en ligne, éditeurs de contenus et services en ligne, ainsi que des acteurs du marketing digital. Leur argument central est que Google a activé ces fonctionnalités en France le 22 juillet 2026 sans concertation
